speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. Tell me, did you develop a new rash or joint pain after finishing your antibiotics for sinusitis? Also, is the flank pain on one side or does it radiate to your groin?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling tired, feverish, and I have flank pain. These symptoms continued even after my sinus symptoms improved.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for confirming those symptoms. To narrow this down, are you experiencing visible jaundice in your eyes or skin, or have you noticed changes in your urine color or frequency?

REQUEST TEST: Liver_Function_Panel, Urinalysis, Blood_Culture

speaker: Patient
text: I was first treated with amoxicillin for sinusitis and developed a rash. Then the antibiotic was changed to cephalexin for another week, and the rash went away. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Pyelonephritis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Drug-induced hypersensitivity interstitial nephritis.

Based on the sequence of events—symptoms appearing after amoxicillin, resolving after switching to cephalexin, followed by re-emergence of flank pain, fever, and fatigue upon re-exposure or progression—the clinical picture strongly suggests an allergic interstitial nephritis rather than typical pyelonephritis. The initial "rash" was likely the first manifestation of this hypersensitivity reaction.
